newsitem.title: UK: North Sea spot and paper crude markets pressured.
newsitem.headline: North Sea spot and paper crude markets pressured.

text.p: North Sea crude markets continued under pressure on Friday, but a slide in Brent paper values left physical Brent cargoes looking slightly more attractive and saw all of today's six Brent dates kept.
"With the Jan/Feb spread trading flat the cargoes are worth hanging onto for the moment," one trader said.
A Jan 18-20 cargo was heard offered down at Feb Brent +5 cents and there was talk of trade for the cargo down to Feb Brent -3 cents but this could not be confirmed.
The Dated Brent market has fallen by around 20 cents this week with trade for third decade Jan barrels slow to develop.

A Brent and an Oseberg, both loading in the third decade, have been fixed to move transatlantic but traders said that Gulf Coast buying was slack and they expected third decade transatlantic trade to be thinner than the second decade.

Other North Sea grades also fetched lower premiums. Forties traded around five cents down at Feb Brent +40 and +41 cents and Oseberg eased five cents to trade at Feb Brent +43 cents. Ekofisk was heard done five to seven cent lower at Feb Brent -18 cents. Statfjord and Gullfaks premiums were also weaker.
Paper markets saw CFDs for next week slump to trade at Feb Brent -5 cents, signalling a further weakening for Dated Brent.
January cargoes of West African crude have been mostly tied up with much of the oil moving transatlantic and to the Far East.
Traders said February barrels were now beginning to move at a steady pace but were mostly being traded as premium to NNPC pricing for February contracts.

Trade was reported at between Feb pricing +$12 to +$16 a barrel depending on quality. Prompt Forcados barrels were assessed steady around 75 cents a barrel over Dated Brent with Bonny light around 65 cents over after trade at +62 cents for a Bonny light-medium and +70 cents for light to the U.S.
Qua Iboe was pegged 55-60 cents over Dated Brent after recent trade at +58 cents with Brass River at the same level.
Cabinda barrels were holding around 60-65 cents a barrel under Dated Brent although traders said the market was looking softer with recent Chinese buying drying up.
In the Mediterranean, Urals crude held steady in balanced trade with limited supplies due to an extended port closure at Novorossiisk countered by a tailing-off in demand from refiners.
Novorossiisk remained shut on Friday due to a heavy swell. The port has been closed since 0850 PM (local time) on Wednesday.
Urals was pegged around $1.10/$1.05 under Dated Brent with around four cargoes traded on Thursday in this range.
